intent: Stop the admission-parity bridge reporting a CANCELLED dependency as a hard failure on a REQUIRED context. Observed twice on 2026-08-07: pr-ci-health supersedes a run whose session-status has starved in the queue, the bridge still runs under always(), and `test cancelled = success` fails. While the queue starves session-status, no PR can earn a green parity check. Skips on cancelled only; always() is retained so a genuine session-status failure still blocks.

negative_controls.name: reverting-the-cancelled-guard-is-caught
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import pathlib,subprocess,sys; p=pathlib.Path('.github/workflows/active-track.yml'); t=p.read_text(); p.write_text(t.replace(\"always() && needs.onboarding-status.result != 'cancelled' &&\",'always() &&',1)); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','-q','tests/test_admission_parity_bridge.py::test_a_cancelled_dependency_does_not_report_as_failure'],check=False); p.write_text(t); sys.exit(0 if r.returncode!=0 else 1)"

commit.message: fix(ci): admission-parity bridge must not read cancelled as failed

interface_mismatches: The bridge's condition decides whether it runs; its body decides pass/fail. A cancelled dependency was reaching the body, where the only vocabulary is success/not-success, so an infrastructure event became a verdict.
honest_blockers: CEREMONY ORDER WAS VIOLATED AND THIS RECEIPT SAYS SO: the fix and its tests were authored before this packet existed. Read the binding as scope CONFORMANCE, not scope-declared-first.

Verified by contract tests over the workflow YAML and two negative controls, NOT by observing a real superseded run go green. The proof that it works is the next cancellation, which I cannot schedule.

A SKIPPED required check counts as success in branch protection. This is safe only because a cancellation implies a newer run exists for the same head. If GitHub ever cancels without a successor, this would convert that into a silent pass.
Does not address the cause: the queue depth that starves session-status for 90 minutes, and the pr-ci-health rebase loop that supersedes it. This only stops the symptom being mislabelled.
session_entry.rollback: Single revert. The bridge returns to reporting cancelled dependencies as failures.
